federation.note: The scheduling-sector RDF model — the data model a Vikunja→Solid fork writes to a pod. MINTS NOTHING: a task is a sched:Task (a core:Activity), a calendar a sched:Calendar, repeats via sched:RecurrenceRule, alarms via sched:Reminder, from @jeswr/solid-federation-vocab's scheduling sector; RSVP status reuses the sector's AttendanceScheme. CROSS-SECTOR (load-bearing): a sched:Task ALSO carries the published @jeswr/solid-task-model wf:Task shape on the SAME subject, so a Vikunja task surfaces 'assigned to me' in Pod Manager / solid-issues — the first external app on the shared task model (the federation-vision demo). As an ONTOLOGY TEST RIG, modelling real Vikunja/kanban task data surfaced scheduling-sector gaps — kanban board/bucket/position (ordering), first-class labels (reuse dct:subject vs mint), the full task-relation set incl. precedes/follows, percent-done, and the sched:CalendarEvent-vs-dav-bridge-schema:Event canonicalisation — written up as fedcon:Proposal CANDIDATES in scheduling.proposals.ttl / DECISIONS.md rather than edited into the sector. Ships a focused SHACL shape + an owner-only fail-closed WAC ACL helper (schedules are owner-private). GitHub-installable now (committed dist/, ignore-scripts=true); npm publish is a deferred migration. The sched:/core: IRIs are legacy w3id.org/jeswr identifiers that re-mint to the jeswr.org persistent-ID layer per the staged migration; fedcon: is already jeswr.org-rooted.
